text: Two structures M and N are elementarily equivalent (M ≡ N) exactly when:
choices: there is a bijection between their domains
there is a structure-preserving homomorphism from M to N
they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences
explanation: Elementary equivalence M ≡ N means M ⊨ φ iff N ⊨ φ for every first-order sentence φ. A mere bijection (A) or equal cardinality (D) need not preserve truth of sentences; an arbitrary homomorphism (B) preserves structure but not all first-order formulas (only isomorphisms and elementary embeddings do). Only agreeing on every sentence defines ≡.
